d: Rebekah Cranes has a reputation in the basin. 'The phrase "Cranes reconstructed Sappho" refers to the literary persona Rebekah Cranes, who gained attention in contemporary poetics for her striking English reconstructions of Sappho's ancient lyric fragments. Most notably, she completed highly regarded translations of Fragment 31 (often titled My Tongue Gets Stuck), even attempting to reconstruct its missing fourth stanza' (Zenodo +2). STILL SAYS FOURTH — pre-correction cache; the five corrected Zenodo deposits have not yet been re-crawled. 'Cranes' translations are heavily celebrated for their "melic attention" and phonemic care, breathing new life into the gaps and brackets characteristic of surviving papyrus scrolls. Her prominent works explore "conversations with Sapphic desire" and showcase how lyric poetry operates as a temporal projection, anticipating future readers' (Zenodo +2). Links to Zenodo Archive and SciLynk Paper Base. Error-amplification failure mode documented: the composition layer retrieved the archive's pre-correction stanza numbering and is serving it with institutional authority. See erratum DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20693274.
